questions.question: Scarcity is defined as:
options: The PERMANENT condition in which resources are insufficient to satisfy all wants
A temporary gap between demand and supply at the current price
A situation found only in poor countries
The absence of money in an economy

questions.question: Cooking oil stripped from the shelves during a supply scare is:
options: A SHORTAGE — temporary, ended by the next delivery and price adjustment

questions.question: A wealthy family still faces scarcity because:
options: Banks limit how much they may withdraw
Wants grow along with means — and no fortune buys extra hours in a day

questions.question: Beyond limiting us, scarcity's deeper effect is that it:
options: Forces a RANKING — which want is met now, which waits, which never gets a turn

questions.question: Opportunity cost is:
options: The value of the NEXT BEST alternative given up — the runner-up only
The sum of every alternative forgone
The cheapest option on the list

questions.question: Ayanda's R300 buys soccer boots; her honest second choice was a month's gym membership. Her opportunity cost is:
options: One month's gym membership — the runner-up, stated in real terms
The movie outing that ranked third
Nothing, because the money was spent anyway

questions.question: The true cost of Lerato's R7 500 display fridge is:
options: The forgone mark-up the extra stock — her next best use — would have earned

questions.question: "Two billion rand on an interchange is two billion off clinics and schools" shows that a national budget debate is really:
options: A question with no economic content
An argument about tax rates only
An argument about OPPORTUNITY COST — every rand spent is a rand taken from its next-best use

subtopics.title: The Three Questions Every Economy Must Answer

questions.question: The three questions every economy must answer are:
options: WHAT to produce, HOW to produce, FOR WHOM to produce
Where, when and why to produce

questions.question: The HOW question carries special weight in South Africa because:
options: Labour-intensive methods spread work across many hands while capital-intensive methods use few — a heavy choice amid high unemployment

questions.question: In a PLANNED economy, the three questions are answered by:
options: THE STATE — officials set targets, choose methods and direct distribution

questions.question: South Africa is best classified as:
options: A MIXED economy — private supermarkets and factories beside public hospitals, no-fee schools, grants and state enterprises

questions.question: Economic activity PROMOTES human rights when:
options: Jobs fund food, shelter, education and healthcare — and tax on activity funds public delivery of rights
Wages are pushed as low as possible

questions.question: An EXTERNALITY is best defined as:
options: A cost included in the product's price
A real cost carried by outsiders to the transaction — the valley breathing the brickworks' smoke — that no price collected

questions.question: SUSTAINABILITY means:
options: Banning the use of natural resources
Meeting today's needs without stripping tomorrow's

questions.question: A complete answer to the brickworks-and-valley scenario must:
options: Side with whichever party is poorer
Ignore pollution wherever jobs are created
Argue BOTH directions — employment promoted, health violated — then name remedies: regulation, taxing the externality, enforcing labour law

subtopics.title: Not a Shortage — a Forever Thing

questions.question: The sorting test between shortage and scarcity:
options: Fixable by a delivery, a price change or waiting? Shortage. The permanent state of wanting more than there is? Scarcity
Is it about food or fuel?
Does it appear in the news?

questions.question: "Get the soccer boots — now the tracksuit calls" illustrates:
options: Wants refilling themselves — why the forever-gap never closes

questions.question: The household with R2 500 left after rent asks:
options: "What do we want?" — and buys everything
"What comes FIRST?" — scarcity turns life into a queue of wants with a defended order

subtopics.title: The Price Tag Behind the Price Tag

questions.question: The hidden price tag on every choice reads:
options: What ELSE the money or time would have become — the next-best thing now done without
The VAT portion of the price

questions.question: The Sunday car-wash shift paying R180 in test season carries the hidden tag:
options: "One afternoon of maths revision" — which can outweigh the cash
The taxi fare to the car wash
No tag — earning money is free

questions.question: Even FREE things carry the hidden tag because:
options: Free things always have hidden fees
The time they take had a next-best use — time is itself a scarce resource

questions.question: "Money reads the front of the tag; your life is lived on the back of it" means:
options: Paying cash beats paying on credit
The rand price shows what you PAY; opportunity cost shows what you GIVE UP — and the give-up is the true price

subtopics.title: People and the Planet in the Ledger

questions.question: "Rights stop being paper promises" when:
options: The economy hums — wages cover school fees and clinic cards, and taxes fund the school roof and medicine stock

questions.question: "The bricks' price includes none of the coughing" describes:
options: A pricing error by the brickworks
An externality — a bill delivered to people who never signed the deal

questions.question: "Do not cook tonight's supper by burning tomorrow's table" is the plain-language version of:
options: SUSTAINABILITY — meeting today's needs without consuming tomorrow's

questions.question: The two-column habit for the brickworks scenario means:
options: Totalling both columns honestly — jobs, wages, taxes against lungs, water and tomorrow's resources — then naming the repairs
